messages.subject: Error using offsets
parts:
HI there

I just found that running the example (below) from the section "Tools to manipulate models and likelihoods" gives the error

Error: length(offset.sum) == NPredictor is not TRUE

 Im getting the same error in other similar situations! The issue seems to be that it is only allowed to have offsets in the linear predictor before applying the linear transformation A! that is A(x+offset)! and not as I think it should be Ax + offset!

Can anyone help?

Thanks

Karim

Here is the code (straight copy + paste from "Tools to manipulate models and likelihoods" )


n = 30

## 'm' is the number of observations of eta~, where eta~ = A eta, and
## A is a fixed m x n matrix.
m = 100

## an offset, just for testing. OOPS: the offset are defined for
## 'eta~' and NOT 'eta'!!!
myoffset = 10+runif(m)

## the covariate
z = runif(n)

## the linear predictor eta
eta = 1 + z

## define it either as matrix, or using sparseMatrix() (in package
## Matrix)
A = matrix(runif(n*m), m, n);
A = as(A, "dgTMatrix")  ## just to test...
Eta = A %*% eta + myoffset
s = 0.0001

## The observations Y can be a sparseMatrix, but there is no need
## to. However, Y will be in this case, as it enherits its properties
## from Eta.
Y = Eta + rnorm(m, sd=s)

r = inla(Y ~ 1+z,

        ## The A-matrix defined here
        control.predictor = list(A=A, compute=TRUE, precision = 1e6),

        ## OOPS: we need to use a list() as the different lengths of Y
        ## and z
        data = list(Y=Y, z=z),

        ## offsets better defined here as in the formula gives the
        ## wrong impression: A formula like y ~ 1 + offset(off)
        ## suggests that the offset is in 'eta', but its in 'eta~'. Be
        ## aware.
        offset = myoffset,

        control.family = list(initial = log(1/s^2), fixed=TRUE))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error using offsets
parts:
On Mon, 2013-01-21 at 16:09 -0800, Karim Anaya wrote:
> HI there
>
>
> I just found that running the example (below) from the section "Tools
> to manipulate models and likelihoods" gives the error
>
>
> Error: length(offset.sum) == NPredictor is not TRUE
>
>
>
> Im getting the same error in other similar situations! The issue
> seems to be that it is only allowed to have offsets in the linear
> predictor before applying the linear transformation A! that is A(x
> +offset)! and not as I think it should be Ax + offset!

Thanks.

There was an internal confusion about the role of an 'offset' in the
formula and the argument of inla(), when an A-matrix is used. This is
now fixed and the example on the web-page is updated.

In short, when an A matrix is used, we have

eta = ... + offset(...)
eta* = A %*% eta + offset.arg

where 'offset(...)' are offsets defined in the formula, whereas
'offset.arg' is the offset defined using the 'offset'-argument,

inla(..., offset = offset.arg)

Hence the two ways of defining the offset has a different role in the
case where the A-matrix is used.

With no A-matrix, then the total offset is simply their sum, so

formule = y ~ ... + offset(a) + offset(b)

inla(formula,..., offset = cc)

then the total offset is 'a + b + cc'


H



--
Håvard Rue
